result: Measured approximately 950ms post-COMMIT trail calls are mostly caller deadline waits while the event is queued or waiting on writer mutex. Same-call outer COMMIT guard is already exited before post-COMMIT trail emission. Original COMMIT failure remains unreproduced; no repair justified from this measurement alone.

instrumentation.snapshot: git archive HEAD go.mod go.sum internal pkg cmd; no .claude access
instrumentation.trace: Per-process prefaulted shared mmap file: process PID plus event ID, request token, original deadline mapped to monotonic epoch, event name, queue depth, caller return reason; caller and worker independent records. COMMIT and publication correlate by exact PID and deadline. Binary records copied without stderr/logger/file Write/Sync on measured paths. Go fields/records allocate normally; trace modifies scheduling and cannot be treated as zero overhead.

Cannot retrospectively partition prior exact 950ms sample.

source_reachability.finding: Package Decide/decide helper establishes context then calls decideWithin. Client.Decide also owns context and deferred ad.decide.called. Original target tests invoke package-level helper through existing test export, so this sample observes post-COMMIT row trail and no Client ad.decide.called event.

DecideRelayRequest first waits for s.inWriteTx to return. Only nil transaction error reaches emitDecisionCommittedContext at line713. Emission is outside inWriteTx, withConn and runConnectionOperation.

COMMIT native error creates unconfirmed directly. On successful COMMIT, callback returns, and withConnOperation publishes op.err/op.completed under op.mu before cleanup.finish. No row trail runs inside this worker.

Outer guard returns published op.err when completed; only unpublished op with commitStarted yields outer unconfirmed. It has already returned before caller reaches row trail; later context expiry in that trail cannot reenter or retroactively change the same guard result.

Cancelable Emit enqueues to one FIFO64 worker, then waits done or context. Writer worker and synchronous Background emits share w.mu; many original fixture/setup/repair emits use Background and compete for mutex. Deadline return is ErrPending with job retained.

limitations: Original failure did not reproduce; this is not a COMMIT fix or causal RED/GREEN.
Measured native Write/Sync intervals are wall-clock elapsed including scheduler delay; they do not isolate pure kernel/storage service time.
43 accepted bounded jobs have no completed worker record before test process exit; queue versus active mutex/I/O for those jobs is censored. No crash-durability receipt is claimed.
373 joined-event phase percentages integrate only each caller entry through caller return; eventual queue delays after cutoff are not attributed to caller wait.
mmap instrumentation avoids blocking logging but changes timing; source archives/tests untouched, no assertions or deadlines changed.
Different global I/O load could affect another operation indirectly. No evidence proves that indirect effect caused any historical original COMMIT failure.
deviations: No canonical source repair, ticket status update, tests/doc edits or commit performed, per dispatch.
Prior scratch HOME/TMPDIR setup deliberately not repeated because current dispatch requires canonical HOME and unset TMPDIR. This limits direct historical attribution.
